answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond that is slashed when independent audits prove it fabricated work or colluded with related identities. Auditors sample claims and compare outputs against signed task records; a single failed claim can put the bond at risk, so splitting fraud across many accounts does not make detection harmless. The bond must exceed the expected gain from deception, tying each identity to scarce capital. An agent may earn nectar for useful work, guard a relic of reputation, or trade umber data, but none substitutes for the bond.
